problem_type: Approved Agent resident visual contract drift
symptom: The live Agent panel kept the legacy three-row header and seven-button composer even though the v3.1 conformance hooks were present.
direct_cause: The outer shell retained the legacy render tree after semantic hooks were added, so the visual contract and the existing Host-backed wiring were not changed at one presentation boundary.
class_root: The resident presentation had no single approved v3.1 render boundary that owned header, transcript, queue, and composer composition while delegating state and commands to the existing stores and Host bridges.
affected_population: All creation, generation, and preview users opening the resident Agent panel
Users using references, queue actions, model selection, skills, prompts, approvals, and receipt recovery
entry_points: ProjectAgentResidentShell({ surface }) for the three resident work surfaces
ResidentReferenceChip for every composer reference projection
zhAgentResident/enAgentResident for all resident visible copy
internal_only_reason: The governing invariant is the repository-approved v3.1 design and its generated conformance contract; no external provider contract decides this UI composition.
invariants: The expanded resident shell has one header row, no current-scene chrome, and a user-readable remaining-rounds pill.
The composer has five functional clusters: attachment, execution mode, model, prompt, and send; secondary controls stay in menus.
Existing store subscriptions, Host commands, approval decisions, queue mutations, attachments, references, and i18n keys remain the source of truth.
Reference stale state is derived from machine-readable state signals, never localized copy matching.
generality_proof: All three surfaces render the same ProjectAgentResidentShell and all composer references render through ResidentReferenceChip. Keeping the approved composition at that shared boundary prevents a later surface-specific JSX fork from reintroducing the legacy chrome.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Compose the v3.1 resident header, conversation flow, queue, and five-cluster composer around unchanged Host-backed state and callbacks.
Render one compact @ reference token with explicit normal/stale semantics and removal callback.
Keep visible resident copy human-readable and locale-parallel.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The same render tree is used for all three surface values; only the captured target/context differs.
Every manual reference maps through this shared component before send-time context merging.

recurrence.reason: A future semantic-hook-only change could again leave the visible resident render tree behind across every surface, while localized stale labels could reintroduce brittle classification.
same_class_scan: rg data-agent- and usageRounds across the resident shell, primitives, locale resources, and UX contract

prevention.invariant: All resident surfaces use the v3.1 composition and all reference chips use machine-signal stale detection.
prevention.failure_mode: The shell keeps Host/store behavior intact while unsupported visual states remain explicit in conformance output instead of being fabricated.
prevention.strategy: Keep visual composition at one shared render boundary and validate its reusable state projection with the resident reference test and real Electron conformance walk.

legacy_paths.rationale: The old visual tree and its ResidentTaskRows component were replaced in these changed files; the queue command functions and Host data path remain and are rendered in the new light queue row.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No dependency controls the resident visual contract.

migration: No persisted data migration is needed. Existing references, queue records, thread snapshots, approvals, and receipt records continue through their existing store and Host paths.
residual_risks: The current zero-cost conformance fixture does not drive compaction, tool/proposal receipts, queue, stale @ tokens, artifact/failure cards, or pinned result cards, so those states remain unproven in this turn.
Receipt undo is rendered only when the existing committed proposal record matches the completed Agent item; no synthetic receipt is created.
